name: Vinted
tagline: Vinted fee calculator: US sellers pay 0% and keep the full sale price; buyers pay a 5% + $0.70 Vinted fee.
fee_summary: Vinted charges US sellers nothing to list or sell: you keep 100% of the item price. The buyer pays shipping plus the Vinted fee, usually $0.70 + 5% of the item price, which is added on top of your price and never comes out of your payout.

sources.title: Vinted Help – Is selling on Vinted free?

inputs.help: The price the buyer agrees to pay for the item (or bundle), before shipping and the buyer's Vinted fee.

inputs.label: What the item cost you
inputs.help: Purchase price or sourcing cost. Enter 0 for things you already owned.

inputs.help: We'll show the price you need to list at to clear this much.

fees.label: Vinted selling fee
fees.note: Vinted charges US sellers no listing fee and no selling fee. You keep 100% of the item price.

fees.label: Vinted fee (paid by buyer)
fees.note: Usually $0.70 plus 5% of the item or bundle price, added to the buyer's total at checkout; Vinted says the calculation can vary with item characteristics, order value and order type. Informational: it does not reduce your payout.

worked_example.explanation: You sell a jacket for $25. Vinted takes no selling fee from US sellers, so your payout is the full $25.00. After the $8 you paid for the jacket, profit is $17.00. The buyer separately pays the Vinted fee, usually $0.70 + 5% of $25 = $1.95, plus shipping, on top of your price; none of that comes out of your $25.

content.intro:
Vinted is a secondhand marketplace for clothing, shoes, accessories, kids' items, and some home goods. Its US pitch is simple: selling is free. Most US sellers are people clearing out closets, alongside a growing number of resellers who prefer a 0% fee to Poshmark's 20% or eBay's roughly 13%.

There is no listing fee, no selling fee, and no payment processing fee for sellers. If your item sells for $25, $25 lands in your Vinted Wallet. Shipping is paid by the buyer, who chooses a carrier option at checkout; you print the prepaid label and drop the package off.

Vinted funds itself on the buyer side. Every order placed with the Buy now button carries a mandatory Vinted fee (formerly called the Buyer Protection fee), usually $0.70 plus 5% of the item price, added automatically at checkout on top of your price and shipping. On a $25 item that is $1.95. Vinted says it helps cover running the platform, member support, and refunds if an item is lost, damaged, or significantly not as described.

Because buyers see your price plus that fee plus shipping, a $25 listing might show as roughly $32 to $35 delivered. Keep that in mind when you price against other apps, and remember that the only seller-paid service on Vinted's US pricelist is the optional item bump, priced in the app before you confirm.
how_fees_work: Selling fee: 0%. Vinted says there are no fees for uploading or selling items and that you keep 100% of what you earn; the only seller-paid service on its US pricelist is the optional item bump. What the buyer pays for the item is what you receive.

Vinted fee (paid by the buyer; formerly the Buyer Protection fee): usually $0.70 plus 5% of the item price, or of the combined bundle price, added automatically at checkout on orders placed with Buy now. Vinted says the calculation varies with item characteristics, order value and whether the order is a single item or a bundle. It does not touch your payout.
Shipping: paid by the buyer, who picks a delivery option at checkout. You get a prepaid label to print. There is no fee to you for the label.
Sales tax: collected from the buyer where required and handled by Vinted; it is not deducted from your price.

Optional promotions: item bumps (3 or 7 days) are the only seller-paid service on the US pricelist. The bump fee depends on the duration, the item price and whether the bump is local or international; it is shown before you confirm and is not a percentage taken from your sales.
Payout: once the sale is successfully closed, the full selling price goes to your Vinted Wallet, and you can transfer it to your bank account.
tips: Price for the buyer's real total. A $25 item costs the buyer $26.95 before shipping because of the usual $0.70 + 5% Vinted fee, so match competitors on the delivered price, not the sticker.
Accept offers freely. With no percentage fee, every dollar you knock off is exactly one dollar less in your pocket, and nothing is lost to commission math.

Bundles help buyers more than you might expect: the $0.70 fixed part of the Vinted fee and shipping are paid once for the whole bundle, so a bundle discount can still leave the buyer paying less per item.
Compare before you cross-list. The same $25 sale nets $25.00 on Vinted, $20.00 on Poshmark, and $23.72 on Depop after its 3.3% + $0.45 processing fee.
Use bumps only for items with proven demand. A bump is a flat charge you pay whether or not the item sells, so it is the one way to lose money on a fee-free platform.

faq.q: Does Vinted charge sellers a fee?
faq.a: No. US sellers pay no listing fee, no selling fee, and no payment processing fee. You keep 100% of the item price.

faq.q: What is the Vinted Buyer Protection fee?
faq.a: Vinted now calls it the Vinted fee: a mandatory fee the buyer pays at checkout, usually $0.70 plus 5% of the item price. It is added on top of the seller's price and does not reduce the seller's payout.
The buyer. They choose a shipping option at checkout and pay for it; the seller prints a prepaid label.

faq.q: How much does Vinted take from a $50 sale?
faq.a: Nothing. You receive $50.00. The buyer pays $50 plus the usual $3.20 Vinted fee ($0.70 + 5%), plus shipping and any sales tax.

faq.q: Why is my Vinted listing price different from what buyers see?
faq.a: Buyers see your price plus the Vinted fee, shipping, and any sales tax. A $25 item shows as $26.95 before shipping.

faq.q: Is there a fee to withdraw money from Vinted?
faq.a: Vinted's US pricelist does not list a withdrawal fee. Proceeds sit in your Vinted Wallet and can be transferred to your bank account; check the app for the current transfer timing.

faq.q: Does Vinted charge sales tax to sellers?
faq.a: No. Where sales tax applies, Vinted collects it from the buyer at checkout as a marketplace facilitator. It is separate from your price.

content.notes: Fee figures come from Vinted's US pricelist (which shows 'Last updated: 10/08/2026') and its 'Vinted fee' help article. Both describe the buyer-paid fee as 'usually 5% + $0.70' and say the calculation varies with item characteristics, order value and order type, so some orders may carry a different buyer fee. The same fee was called the Buyer Protection fee when this page was first written, and the help article's address still uses that name. The pricelist's only seller-paid service is the item bump, whose price varies and is shown before purchase, so it is not modeled; Wardrobe Spotlight, which this page used to mention, is not on the US pricelist. Payout timing and bank-transfer details were not verified on an official page for this update. Fees differ in other Vinted countries.
